rv.q: Watching Gough in People, Places & Things has a similar effect: exhilarating and scary. You don't quite expect just how much your bones are going to shudder with the blast.
Though the play is about her gruesome, last-ditch efforts to get clean, her plight is never less than damnably entertaining.
As a production and a performance, People, Places & Things is a fireworks display.
The remainder of this harrowing play's two hours lives up to this devastating beginning.
Herrin's invigorating production is unlike anything we've ever seen in terms of sheer creativity.
It was also one of the most moving scenes I've experienced this season.

Like the play that barely contains her, Gough’s performance keeps you riveted at every turn, even as her character is practically on a continuous roller-coaster ride–a ride which she takes us on with her, as she plays out her tenacious addiction to drugs and alcohol.

Denise Gough, the lead actor, isn't just good. She's great playing Emma, an actress-addict who just can't stop imbibing every drug known to man and swilling it down with the nearest alcoholic beverage.
Gough is transfixing, and to miss her in this would be a crime.
Just when you think 'you've seen it all' on the topic of drug addiction and recovery, along comes a play that blows the top of your head off.
